name: Google Workspace MCP
description: Ports agentic-workspace's aw-google-workspace integration into aw-workspace: runs the community workspace-mcp server (taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp) as a managed background service and registers it with MCP Gateway, giving every agent Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Tasks and Contacts tools behind one Google OAuth token.

skills.description: Full Google Workspace access (Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Tasks, Contacts) through this app's workspace-mcp server on the aw-gateway — tool overview, the OAuth flow when a call says authorization is needed, and the attachment/path rule that avoids base64 corruption.

google_oauth_client_id.description: OAuth 2.0 client ID for the Google Cloud project this server authenticates against. Ported from agentic-workspace's src/config/mcp.json (the dedicated "Workspace MCP" Desktop-app client in the `crispal` project). Not a credential on its own, so it rides plain app config and is visible in Settings.

google_oauth_client_secret.description: OAuth 2.0 client secret matching the client ID above. Routed to the zero-knowledge secret store via POST /api/apps/google-workspace-mcp/settings — never stored in plain config, same pattern as aw-app-notion's notion_token.

user_google_email.description: Default Google account. The server runs with --single-user, so every tool call falls back to this address when `user_google_email` is not passed explicitly, and its OAuth token file is <credentials dir>/<email>.json.

tools.default: gmail drive calendar contacts docs sheets tasks
tools.description: Space-separated tool groups to register, passed straight to `workspace-mcp --tools`. Ported verbatim from the monolith. Valid: appscript, calendar, chat, contacts, docs, drive, forms, gmail, search, sheets, slides, tasks. Adding a group needs the server restarted (Settings → Restart server).

port.description: Port workspace-mcp binds inside the workspace container, serving Streamable HTTP at /mcp. 8010 is the monolith's value (8000 was already taken there). Reachable only on the container network — MCP Gateway connects to it by container hostname; nothing is published to the host.

allowed_file_dirs.description: Directories send_gmail_message's `attachments: [{path: ...}]` may read from (ALLOWED_FILE_DIRS). The monolith pointed this at /opt/agentic-workspace/.tmp; here it is the equivalent workspace scratch dir, so screenshots and exports can be attached by path instead of base64 — see the skill for why base64 attachments silently corrupt.

oauth_redirect_uri.description: Optional override for the OAuth callback URL (GOOGLE_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI). Leave empty to use http://localhost:<port>/oauth2callback, which is what the ported Desktop-app OAuth client expects. Set this only if you switch to a Web-app OAuth client with a publicly reachable callback.

pin_version.description: PyPI version of `workspace-mcp` installed into this app's own private venv. Pinned on purpose: the package pulls its own starlette/cryptography/mcp/fastmcp versions, which is exactly why it must never share the workspace's venv (that broke the monolith once).

apps.reason: This app contributes an mcp.json entry (the 'google-workspace' server) that MCP Gateway discovers and merges; without the gateway the server runs but no agent can reach its tools.

dependencies.note: Runtime-enforced app dependency: aw-workspace loads mcp-gateway before this app so the gateway can scan google-workspace-mcp/mcp.json.
